lessonPlan.topic: Student Book   p.25 - A Listen, point and say

details: Listen, point and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows students can  match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear sounds and confident repetition.
“Today we’re going to the farm!  Can you see the animals! Can you smell them? (Mime sniffing). Can you help me say the names of the animals!?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book   p.25 - B. Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle continues checking sound–image connection and fine motor skills. Students practise listening for specific information and clearly circling an image.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices, pencil grip and penmanship.
“Oh no! I’m not sure all the animals are here. Have some escaped? We need to check. Let’s listen and circle all the names!”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.26 - C. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language, in this case the contracted forms of ‘what is’ and ‘it is' plus the singular ‘this’, to ask and respond to simple questions.

Look for correct formation of the question, particularly the /ɒ/ sound and the ‘s’ of the contracted ‘is’. Identification of the correct animal in the answer, correct formation of ‘it’s’ and correct pronunciation and authentic intonation.
“I’m confused. What has happened to the animals? I can’t see them. I can only see white shapes. Can you tell me the names of the animals?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.26 - D. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language, in this case the contracted form of ‘they’re' plus the plural ‘these’, to ask and respond to simple questions.

Look for correct formation of the question form, particularly the long /i/ sound in ‘these’ (contrasting with the short  /ɪ/ sound in ‘this’) and  correct pronunciation of ‘they’re’ and the plural form in the answer. Encourage authentic intonation in both the question and the answer.
“The animals are playing a game and  hiding (mime hiding behind your hands) from us!. Let’s look for thm.! I think I can see them – can you see them? Let’s ask!”

As well as being fun, the chant gives students the chance to practise the natural rhythms and intonation of the language in an authentic context.
Look for active participation, correct pronunciation, authentic intonation and all students participating.
“Great job - we’ve found  all the animals! Let’s check they’re all here! Are you ready to sing?”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
